headline: Yadgir faces severe child stunting at 44.7%, with 405 malnourished children identified in 2024 survey amid poverty challenges
summary: Yadgir district confronts alarming child undernutrition, with 44.7% stunting far above Karnataka's 27.9% average. A 2024 survey identified 405 undernourished children across three taluks, with figures expected to rise. Officers cite abject poverty preventing children from receiving even two square meals daily despite anganwadi centres providing nutritious food to 1.39 lakh children. The 2022 Human Development Report flagged Yadgir among Karnataka's districts where nutrition is a major concern, alongside persistent poverty affecting over 20% of the population.

reasons.detail: Officers cite poverty as main reason for malnutrition, with children receiving only one anganwadi meal unable to access adequate food at home
Among 9,910 children screened and referred for treatment between April 2025-May 2026, only 1,189 received care, leaving 8,721 untreated

modelFactorWhy.why: Yadgir had the highest number of children without pre-school education access, prompting a dedicated programme to improve anganwadi attendance and quality. Poor educational outcomes persist, with Yadgir recording the state's lowest PUC pass rate at 48.45% in 2024-25.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Pre-school attendance provides structured nutrition through anganwadis, early health monitoring, and developmental support critical for preventing stunting during formative years.

modelFactorWhy.factor: Household members covered by health insurance
modelFactorWhy.why: The available pages contain no information about health insurance coverage rates among Yadgir households. However, they document severe healthcare access problems: 8,721 children referred for treatment received none, suggesting broader systemic healthcare barriers beyond insurance.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Health insurance enables families to afford preventive care, treatment for childhood illnesses, and maternal services, reducing financial barriers that contribute to malnutrition and stunting.

proof.claim: Of 9,910 children screened and referred for treatment, only 1,189 received medical care, leaving 8,721 untreated

modelFactorWhy.factor: Mothers who took iron-folic acid for 180+ days in pregnancy
modelFactorWhy.why: The pages do not provide data on iron-folic acid supplementation during pregnancy in Yadgir. They do note that adolescent mothers face elevated risks of anemia and that health screenings identified widespread anemia among children, suggesting maternal nutrition gaps.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Iron-folic acid supplementation during pregnancy prevents maternal anemia and supports fetal growth, directly reducing risk of low birth weight and subsequent stunting in children.

proof.claim: Adolescent mothers face elevated risks of anemia, preterm births, and maternal mortality
